answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The cedar multiplier is published, charged in juniper, and lagoon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3823 identities would post 1935 proofs and burn roughly 75 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
